findings.passage: It is Day Three of the 2025-2026 legislative session. Already, Republicans skirted the rules and rushed senators into a senate floor session. Republicans are more afraid of voters and losing power than they are about the issues that are impacting those voters.
findings.note: Press release issued in his name, stating his opposition to 2025 Senate Joint Resolution 2 (the voter ID constitutional amendment) during the Senate floor session. The quoted text objects to how the session was handled and does not discuss ID requirements themselves. Also carried by WEAU (https://www.weau.com/2025/01/08/wisconsin-gop-lawmakers-looking-get-voter-id-laws-state-constitution-by-spring/).

findings.passage: As a gun owner, I firmly believe in an individual’s right to own a firearm. I also believe gun violence prevention is long overdue.
findings.note: From his signed op-ed 'Gun Control Has Wide Support' (State Sen. Jeff Smith, Urban Milwaukee). States he owns a gun, supports the individual right to own one, and supports gun violence prevention.

findings.passage: Polls consistently show people from all walks of life and political views favoring universal background checks. Wisconsin is ready for commonsense gun violence reforms, so why aren’t Republican lawmakers?
findings.note: From the same op-ed. Cites polls for universal background checks and calls for gun violence reforms. He also cites poll numbers on a ban on assault-style weapons and a high-capacity magazine ban, without stating his own view on those in that passage.

findings.passage: If the NRA wants to explain why simple background checks are wrong, or why they believe the founders thought it was necessary to have high-capacity magazines and assault-style weapons when drafting the 2nd Amendment then let them try.
findings.note: From the same op-ed. Challenges the argument that the Second Amendment blocks background checks, high-capacity magazine limits and assault-style weapon limits.

findings.passage: Would a temporary law enforcement firearm removal order, also called a “red flag law,” stop this horribly tragic event? We’ll never know.
findings.note: From the same op-ed. Raises the red-flag law as a question about one shooting; later in the piece he relays a gun shop owner favoring a properly worded red flag law and says 'We can own guns responsibly and still demand action for gun violence.'
